sections.title: One truck, one trailer, and a lot of *faith*

image.alt: A Beech Island Timber Kenworth loaded with logs

body: Josh T. Key fell for logging as a teenager, working for his uncle's logging company. He started on his own with a single truck and trailer, hauling timber as an owner-operator, and together with his wife Cindy built the company the two of them still own and operate today.

We employ 15 to 20 hard-working men and women, and most of them have been with us for more than ten years. That experience shows up on your land: in swamps, on hills and on level ground, with chip-n-saw, pulpwood, hardwood and saw timber.
list: Family owned and operated in Jackson, SC
Serving Aiken, Augusta, Jackson and the Savannah River Site area
Safe Work Activities Recognition, Ameresco Federal Solutions, 2009

sections.title: Harvested the *right way*

image.alt: A John Deere skidder working among standing pines

body: Best Management Practices are simple techniques that reduce erosion and keep soil out of streams. Many of our employees are trained and certified under South Carolina's BMP program, and we are SFI certified under the Sustainable Forestry Initiative.

We plan ahead so that road and deck locations, skid trails and water crossings all follow the BMP method. You get peace of mind that your timberland is in the hands of a well-trained, experienced and dedicated crew.
list: Water quality and erosion standards met on every tract
Roads, decks and skid trails planned in advance
Work completed on schedule, with precision

sections.title: Join *Team Beech Island*

image.alt: The Beech Island Timber crew in safety vests

body: Our success depends on skilled, motivated people, and safety comes first in everything we do. We treat every employee with respect, dignity and trust, which is why so many stay with us for the long haul.

Positions that come available include equipment operators (skidder, cutter, loader) and truck drivers within a 75-mile radius. Owner-operators with chip vans or log trailers are welcome to get on file as subcontractors. Send your resume to Shelley K. Bowman by email, or fax it to (803) 302-1126.
